scope: Fresh local native-renderer OS/Node/embedded-Go vulnerability inventory and supported-base remediation; no deployment. All remaining matches stay visible.
result: OPEN upstream limitations: 40 OS package/advisory matches, 27 unique CVEs; 34 Ubuntu MEDIUM and 6 Ubuntu LOW; no vendor FixedVersion. Final Node package inventory has zero indexed advisories.

scanner.privacy: Only official tool/base-image/CVE database and public vendor metadata downloads; scans use the local Docker image by immutable ID. No image/private source upload service; telemetry, remote fallback and dependency-resolution lookups disabled.

remediation: Preserve exact pinned Playwright Chromium headless and Node binaries, use supported Ubuntu 26.04 runtime with only official Chromium dependencies and fonts, apply available apt upgrades, keep dpkg metadata.
Remove unused browser distributions, GStreamer/media packages and all npm build-time dependency trees by not copying them into final runtime.
Remove unused /usr/bin/pebble Go binary after direct package-ownership check showed no dpkg owner; this removes its sole fixable embedded-Go advisory without removing package metadata.

Actually build and native-test supported Debian 13 slim alternative; its current vendor feed reports 450 OS matches including 1 CRITICAL and 121 HIGH, so retain the lower-exposure supported Ubuntu 26.04 option.
Bind actual container renderer script SHA-256 to the current repository source in a new native integration invariant and retag only the tested immutable final image.

validation.checks: Actual native rendering, interaction/network denial/resource safety plus nonroot minimal-runtime inventory and exact renderer source hash bridge. See test source and log for full assertions.

limitations: All 40 remaining OS matches are OPEN. No supported vendor FixedVersion was present in the scanned current Ubuntu packages/database; vendor pages independently show Vulnerable or Vulnerable, fix deferred for every affected source package.

Ubuntu-selected severities are contextual vendor ratings, not the maximum upstream/NVD CVSS. Some remaining CVEs have higher upstream scores; this is not a claim that all high-CVSS issues disappeared.

The exact Node and Chrome binaries are copied from the pinned official Playwright image and their versions/hashes match the original. OS/Node-package scanning does not comprehensively attest vulnerabilities in these standalone native binaries.
Runtime context mitigations are not a formal exploitability proof, particularly graphics/font/XML parsers processing untrusted renderer content.
Actual build/native tests were performed on linux/arm64. Playwright lists supported Ubuntu26/Debian13 x64 and arm64 dependencies, but amd64 was not executed in this audit.
No kernel/host/Colima security attestation, fuzzing of native browser internals, or deployment occurred.
Database and apt repository state are time-bound; rerun builds and scans when vendor updates arrive.

upstream_release_advisory_check.scope: Compact read-only primary-source release/advisory check; no new full binary CVE scan, no input changes.

node.date_note: Official distribution index dates the entry 2026-11-10; release/security blog is dated 2026-11-11. Both refer to v26.13.1.
node.security_status: Official release labels v26.13.1 a security release and lists fixes for current TLS, HTTPS and HTTP/2 advisories. Security index latest observed post is November 11. No newer26.x release was present in the fetched index.

playwright.advisory_limit: Official repository advisory endpoint returned an empty array. This is not a claim that the product has never had vulnerabilities or that all advisories must appear in that repository endpoint.

chrome.release_status: Exact installed version is the current Beta listed by the official Chrome for Testing feed. Dev and Canary160 entries also exist; they are different release channels, not an established required security patch for the current bundled Beta.
chrome.stable_security_review: Read official November9 and November11 stable security posts. November9 includes actively exploited CVE-2026-125350, fixed in the157 stable update; November11 lists additional fixes. These stable posts do not independently enumerate every fix present or absent in this159 Beta binary, so no comprehensive cross-branch patch-equivalence claim is made.

upstream_release_advisory_check.conclusion: No newer same-line Node release, newer Playwright release or newer Beta browser build was found in these official snapshots, and no concrete actionable vulnerability in the exact installed versions was established by this compact check. This is not zero-CVE attestation; standalone binary and cross-branch patch-coverage limits remain open.
